theater: 印度河流域西北岸與犍陀羅

battle.name: 塞琉古-孔雀戰爭
battle.theater: 印度河流域西北岸與犍陀羅
battle.brief: 公元前305年至前303年，塞琉古一世東進越過印度河，與旃陀羅笈多治下的孔雀帝國在西北邊境相撞，最終以割地、聯姻與五百頭戰象換來和平。卡面這件亞述長矛代表的，是亞述人開創的鐵鏃長矛路線：塞琉古方陣倚仗的加長長矛，正是它的希臘化版本。會戰細節並無記載，勝負只在條約裡分曉。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 塞琉古-孔雀戰爭是公元前305年至前303年間，塞琉古王國與孔雀帝國在印度河東岸及西北邊境之間的一場邊境衝突，也是亞歷山大帝國崩解之後，東西兩方勢力第一次在同一條河流上劃界。交戰的一方是孔雀帝國：旃陀羅笈多（希臘史料作 Sandrocottus）大約在公元前321年前後於西北印度起兵，以十一年征伐推翻難陀王朝、攻下華氏城，在摩揭陀重建了一個以中央集權、省級官制與常備軍為骨架的帝國，疆域自印度河下游與犍陀羅伸向德干與孟加拉，軍隊主力是長矛步兵、弓手、象兵與戰車，另有國王直轄的象隊。另一方是塞琉古王國：塞琉古一世尼卡托在後繼者戰爭中取得美索不達米亞、波斯、帕提亞、巴克特里亞、索格底亞、阿拉科西亞、亞美尼亞與所謂塞琉古的卡皮多細亞等東方總督區，國界一度直抵印度河，軍隊以馬其頓方陣為骨架，配備加長長矛的方陣、騎兵、象兵與各類傭兵，靠總督區的資源與對外盟邦維持東線。塞琉古的指揮系統是國王加總督加營將，命令靠傳令與號角下達；孔雀一方是國王加省長（mandas）加軍事統帥，雖無希臘式總參謀部，卻能以大量訓練有素的步兵與象群守住東線。兩國規模、傳統與制度幾乎全然不同，卻在同一條河邊第一次面對面，這場戰爭的軍事規模不大，意義卻遠大於戰鬥本身。
countriesEn: The Seleucid–Mauryan War was a border clash between the Seleucid kingdom and the Mauryan empire fought along the Indus and its northwestern frontier between 305 and 303 BC, and it was the first time after the collapse of Alexander's empire that two powers of the East and the West drew a frontier on the same river. One side was the Mauryan empire. Chandragupta (Sandrocottus in the Greek sources) rose in northwestern India around 321 BC, spent eleven years of campaigning overturning the Nanda dynasty and taking Pataliputra, and rebuilt from Magadha an empire with a centralised administration, provincial governors and a standing army, whose extent reached from the lower Indus and Gandhara down to the Deccan and Bengal, its strength lying in spearmen, archers, elephants and chariots, with a royal herd of war elephants at the centre. The other side was the Seleucid kingdom. Seleucus I Nicator had won Mesopotamia, Persis, Parthia, Bactria, Sogdia, Arachosia, Hyrcania, Armenia and the so-called Seleucid Cappadocia during the Wars of the Diadochi, and his frontier at its height reached the Indus itself; his army was a Hellenistic force with a Macedonian phalanx at its core, supported by cavalry, elephants and mercenaries of many kinds, and the king held the east together through satrapies and through alliances among the Diadochi, Antigonids and Ptolemies. The Seleucid chain of command was king, satrap and camp officer, orders travelling by messenger and horn; the Mauryan side ran king, provincial governor and military commander, and although it had no Hellenistic general staff, it could field massed infantry and a great many war elephants to hold the eastern line. The two states differed in almost every respect of scale, tradition and institutions, yet here they faced one another for the first time on the same river; the military scale of the war was small, but its meaning was far larger than the fighting.
people: 這場戰爭留下的人名不多，但每個名字都指向具體的決策。塞琉古一方是塞琉古一世尼卡托，即希臘史料中的塞琉古斯·尼卡托爾：他在亞歷山大死後的後繼者戰爭中被逐出東方，公元前308年在阿里俄斯河擊敗安條克三世而奪回東土，隨後把視線投向印度河以東那些名義上仍屬於他的總督區。孔雀一方是旃陀羅笈多，希臘人稱 Sandrocottus 或 Sandracottos，在查士丁的編年裡又寫作 Chandracottos；他大約在公元前321年前後起兵，十一年後滅難陀王朝而定都華氏城，此時已是南亞唯一有資格與塞琉古平手較量的君主。直接參戰者多數無名，但可以分辨出幾類角色：孔雀王朝的省級將領與象隊指揮，替國王管訓象夫、挑選獸群並編成的專職人員；塞琉古方面的方陣營將、騎兵指揮與傭兵首領；以及從希臘本土、波斯與中亞來的軍需商人與譯員——邊界上每一次丈量土地、每一次交換俘虜、每一次把兩套度量衡對上，都要靠這些人把兩種制度接在一起。留下記載的四位作者同樣關鍵：斯特拉博、普魯塔克、阿庇安與尤尼安努斯·查士丁都提到這場交鋒或這條條約，Jansari 指出斯特拉博與普魯塔克很可能同出一源，甚至可能來自塞琉古派駐華氏城的使者梅加斯梯尼所寫的《印度志》——一部已經失傳的書。梅加斯梯尼同時留下對華氏城尺寸、城牆與門數的描述，是唯一能用來對照孔雀帝國首都規模的數字。真正決定戰局走向的，還有那些沒有留下姓名的選擇：誰決定越過印度河，誰決定接受劃界，誰決定把五百頭象交出去。
peopleEn: Few names survive from this war, but each one points at a specific decision. On the Seleucid side there is Seleucus I Nicator, Seleucus Nikator of the Greek sources, who was driven out of the east during the Wars of the Diadochi after Alexander's death, defeated Antiochus III at the river Arius in 308 BC to recover the eastern provinces, and then turned his eye on the satrapies east of the Indus that still nominally belonged to him. On the Mauryan side there is Chandragupta, called Sandrocottus or Sandracottos by the Greeks and written Chandracottos in Justin's chronicle; he rose around 321 BC, and eleven years later had overthrown the Nandas and made Pataliputra his capital, by which time he was the only ruler in South Asia entitled to be matched against Seleucus. Most of those who actually fought leave no name, but several kinds of figure can be distinguished: the provincial commanders and elephant-officers of the Mauryan court, together with the specialists who trained mahouts, selected the herds and formed the units; the phalanx camp officers, cavalry commanders and mercenary captains of the Seleucid side; and the quartermasters and interpreters who came from Greece, Persia and Central Asia. On the frontier, every survey of land, every exchange of prisoners and every reconciliation of two systems of weights and measures depended on these men to hold the two institutions together. The four authors who recorded the matter matter just as much: Strabo, Plutarch, Appian and Junianus Justinus all mention the encounter or the treaty, and Jansari points out that Strabo and Plutarch probably drew on a common source, perhaps the Indica written by Megasthenes, the Seleucid envoy resident at Pataliputra, a book now lost. Megasthenes also left the description of the size of Pataliputra, its wall and its gates, the only figures with which the scale of the Mauryan capital can be compared. What really decided the course of the war were the decisions that left no names: who chose to cross the Indus, who chose to accept a demarcation, who chose to hand over five hundred elephants.
kits: 卡面這件亞述長矛，是亞述人給兩河流域留下的短柄長刃鐵鏃：短握柄、長刃口，既可近身捅刺，也可擲出，亞述人把它同弓與鐵箭鏢綁在一起，讓兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落，也因此留下早期世界最完整的一套矛、弓與鐵的組合。公元前305年至前303年的塞琉古-孔雀邊界戰爭裡，亞述式的短矛不會整批出現在陣前，但這件卡面兵器所代表的技術路線不但沒有斷，還在兩個軍團裡各走了一段：一端是塞琉古方陣的加長長矛（sarissa），兩手持握、桿後段帶鐵配重、矛頭為窄刃鐵，其做法正是亞述人把鐵鏢頭安在木桿上的那一條路；另一端是孔雀軍隊的長矛步兵，手持比希臘方陣矛略短但同樣是鐵鏃的長矛，配木胎蒙皮方盾，隊形偏向密集的步兵方陣，而非線形長矛牆。孔雀一方最具決定性的裝備其實是象：五百頭亞洲象經專人馴養，背負木製戰鬥台，上面立弓手與槍手，前方由象夫引導、槍手執長矛護衛；象群能撞散密集陣線，也能在沒有道路的河灘與鹽灘上充當運輸主力。弓箭方面，孔雀帝國以竹木複合弓配鐵箭為主，弓手數量極大，陣前以縱射覆蓋敵軍接近線；希臘方陣則靠投射標槍與弓手掩護前排展開。雙方都有車，孔雀軍的戰車多由四馬牽引、上立乘兵與旗手，塞琉古的車隊更輕，負責追擊與傳令。馬匹同樣關鍵：孔雀王朝從犍陀羅一線取得良馬，馬政是東線軍力的瓶頸之一，而印度又是地中海世界唯一能供應戰象的地方，這正是這場戰爭真正的交易品。運輸與補給靠河流與陸路配合：印度河既是分界線，也是季風航運的主軸；塞琉古軍隊的糧食多靠沿途總督區徵收，孔雀軍隊則靠摩揭陀的稻米與恆河、印度河的水陸聯運。
kitsEn: The Assyrian spear on the card is the short-hafted, long-bladed iron head left to Mesopotamia by the Assyrians: a short grip and a long edge, serviceable both for thrusting at close quarters and for throwing, tied by the Assyrians together with the bow and iron arrowheads so that the cities of Mesopotamia fell one after another, and so that the oldest world combined arms of spear, bow and iron was made complete. In the Seleucid–Mauryan border war of 305 to 303 BC the Assyrian short spear was not marching in formed lines, but the technical tradition this card represents was not broken; it ran on in two different directions in two different armies. One was the long sarissa of the Seleucid phalanx, held in both hands, with an iron butt-spike behind the shaft and a narrow iron head, following exactly the Assyrian practice of fitting an iron blade to a wooden shaft. The other was the long spear of the Mauryan infantry, somewhat shorter than the Hellenistic phalanx spear but iron-headed in the same way, carried with a wooden shield covered in hide, and drawn up in dense infantry blocks rather than in a linear wall of long spears. The most decisive piece of Mauryan equipment, however, was the elephant. Five hundred Asian elephants, trained by specialists, carried wooden fighting platforms on which archers and lancers stood, led at the front by their mahouts and guarded by spearmen; they could break dense formations, and they could serve as the main means of transport across river flats and salt flats where no road ran. In archery the Mauryan empire relied on composite bows of bamboo and wood with iron arrows, and its numbers of archers were very great, covering the approach of any enemy with massed volleys; the Hellenic phalanx relied on javelins and on archers to cover the deployment of its front rank. Both sides used chariots: Mauryan chariots were usually drawn by four horses and carried a fighting man and a standard-bearer, while the lighter Seleucid vehicles were used for pursuit and for carrying messages. Horses were equally critical; the Mauryan state drew good horses from the Gandharan side, and the horse supply was one of the bottlenecks of the eastern armies, while India remained the only place from which the Mediterranean world could obtain war elephants, and that was the real article being traded in this war. Transport and supply worked river and road together: the Indus was at once the frontier and the axis of monsoon navigation; the Seleucid army drew its grain largely by levy from the satrapies it passed through, while the Mauryan army drew on the rice of Magadha and on the combined water and land traffic of the Ganges and the Indus.
tactics: 關於作戰過程，現存史料幾乎一片空白：斯特拉博、阿庇安、普魯塔克與查士丁都只留下渡過印度河、與 Sandrocottos 交戰、然後達成協議與聯姻這一類骨架，沒有任何一位作者描述過會戰的部署。因此戰術只能從兩軍的體制與地理反推。孔雀軍隊的打法接近亞述式密集步兵的放大版：長矛步兵在前列成方陣，弓手在後與兩翼成排射擊，車隊與象群編在方陣之後與兩翼；象群一旦逼近，會用長鼻與套在鼻端的鐵件撞散對方正面，把對手從陣線上撕開，隨後由步兵與車兵湧入缺口。希臘方陣則需要開闊平地才能展開加長長矛的縱深，一旦地形狹窄、河道切割或山脊起伏，加長長矛便由優勢變成累贅——這既是塞琉古在印度河東岸的可乘之機，也是他最終選擇談判而非決戰的地理理由。印度河在公元前305年是一道實質障礙：河道寬處可行軍，汛期與上游雪水又令渡口變幻莫測；再往西是馬克蘭海岸的鹽灘與沙漠，馬蘭山脈連亞歷山大都曾為穿越它付出高昂代價。可動用的作戰季節被季風切斷，冬季與雨季不適合跨越印度河上游，這使任何越河戰役都必須在狹窄的窗口內完成。雙方的後勤同樣決定節奏：孔雀軍隊遠在摩揭陀，越過德干高原與印度河平原的補給線極長；塞琉古軍隊已深入無名之地，沒有就地徵發就寸步難行。雙方高明的地方，是把戰爭停在會戰之前：孔雀守住了已有的河東江山，塞琉古沒有貿然強渡，而是用割地、聯姻與五百頭象換取西線的準備時間。這是一場以交換代替決戰的邊界戰爭。
tacticsEn: On the conduct of the fighting the surviving record is almost blank. Strabo, Appian, Plutarch and Justin all preserve only a skeleton: crossing the Indus, making war on Sandrocottos, and then coming to an agreement and a marriage. Not one of them describes a deployment, and the tactics can therefore only be reasoned back from the organisation of the two armies and from the geography. The Mauryan way of fighting was an enlarged version of the dense Assyrian infantry: spearmen in the front rank formed blocks, archers fired in ranks behind and on both flanks, and the chariots and elephants were posted behind the blocks and on the wings. Once the elephants closed, they would break the opposing front with their trunks and the iron fitted to them, tearing the enemy off his line, and infantry and chariotry would then pour into the gap. The Hellenic phalanx, by contrast, needed open ground on which to deploy the depth of the long sarissa; where the ground was narrow, cut by a river or broken by ridges, the long spear became a liability instead of an advantage. That was both the opening available to Seleucus on the eastern bank of the Indus and the geographical reason why he finally chose negotiation rather than a pitched battle. The Indus in 305 BC was a real obstacle: there were places where the river could be forded, but the flood and the melting of the snows upstream made the fords unpredictable, and further west lay the salt flats and desert of the Makran coast, while the Malan range had cost Alexander dearly to cross. The usable campaigning season was cut by the monsoon, and neither winter nor the rains suited a crossing of the upper Indus, so any campaign across the river had to be completed inside a narrow window. Logistics set the tempo on both sides. The Mauryan army stood far away in Magadha, and its line of supply across the Deccan plateau and the Indus plain was long; the Seleucid army was deep in a country without names, and could not move a step without requisitioning on the spot. What was skilful on both sides was the decision to stop the war before a pitched battle. The Mauryan kept the country east of the river they already held, and Seleucus did not force a crossing: he bought the time he needed in the west with territory, a marriage and five hundred elephants. This was a border war settled by exchange instead of by decision on the field.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。其一是年代：中文的戰爭列表把此役繫於公元前305年，主流研究則把交鋒放在公元前305年至前303年之間，並常以公元前303年作為割地契約的時間點；史家 V. A. 史密斯在1914年的《印度早期史》中即採前303年之說，坦恩（Tarn, 1922）則以地誌考證了割地的實際邊界。公元前308年塞琉古一世在阿里俄斯河擊敗安條克三世、收回東土，是這場戰爭的直接前奏。其二是距離與地望：印度河全長約三千二百公里，是世界上最長的河流之一；帕羅帕米薩德與帕羅帕米斯山即今興都庫什山脈，構成北界；犍陀羅在今巴基斯坦西北，阿拉科西亞即坎大哈，阿里亞即赫拉特，伽得羅西亞即馬克蘭沿岸。割讓的界線據坦恩考證，大致沿波拉利—欣戈爾河一線，即今巴基斯坦俾路支省境內的山脈與河道分界；亞歷山大當年穿越馬蘭山脈的艱難，因此不只是傳說。其三是物量與城市：斯特拉博引梅加斯梯尼記載，華氏城長約九又二分之一斯台亞、寬約一又二分之一斯台亞，木柵有五百七十座門，磚牆高約六又二分之一斯台亞、厚約二斯台亞；同一段文字說國王取土地產的六分之一；而這場交割的核心物是五百頭戰象，那是印度向希臘世界唯一的戰略物種出口。人口與傷亡數字無從核實：所有記載都出自同一個希臘文傳統，沒有任何一份文獻給出交戰雙方的兵力，也沒有提到任何一場會戰，因此所謂孔雀軍出動數十萬人一類說法沒有可靠依據。唯一可以確定的，是它的量級：這是一場邊境衝突，不是全面戰爭。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is chronology: the Chinese list of battles ties this war to 305 BC, while mainstream scholarship places the confrontation between 305 and 303 BC and often takes 303 BC as the date of the cession; V. A. Smith, in his Early History of India of 1914, already used 303 BC, and Tarn in 1922 checked the actual frontier of the cession against the geography of the country. The battle of the Arius in 308 BC, in which Seleucus I defeated Antiochus III and recovered the eastern provinces, is the immediate prelude. The second class is distance and place. The Indus is about three thousand two hundred kilometres long and among the longest rivers in the world; the Paropamisadae and the Paropamisus range, that is the Hindu Kush, form the northern edge; Gandhara lies in what is now northwestern Pakistan, Arachosia is Kandahar, Aria is Herat, and Gedrosia is the Makran coast. The line of cession, as Tarn established it, runs broadly along the Porali–Hingol river, that is along a watershed and a watercourse inside what is now the Pakistani province of Baluchistan, so the difficulty Alexander had in crossing the Malan range was never only a story. The third class is quantities and cities. Strabo, citing Megasthenes, describes Pataliputra as about nine and a half stadia long and one and a half wide, with a wooden palisade of five hundred and seventy gates and a brick wall about six and a half stadia high and two stadia thick; the same passage says the king took a sixth of the produce of the land; and the central object of the whole transaction was five hundred war elephants, the one strategic animal the Indian world could export to the Greek one. No figure for population or for losses can be checked at all: all the accounts come from a single Greek literary tradition, no document gives the size of either army, and no battle is mentioned, so statements about hundreds of thousands of Mauryan men have no reliable basis. The only thing certain is the order of magnitude. This was a border conflict, not a general war.
cause: 打起來有四層原因。最深的一層是亞歷山大留下的真空：公元前323年他死後帝國被繼承者瓜分，印度河上游那些由馬其頓人與希臘人治理的總督區一時成了無主之地，希臘文獻記載印度人像甩掉奴役的包袱一樣暗殺了自己的總督，秩序隨之崩潰，旃陀羅笈多正是在這個亂局裡於西北印度起兵，經十一年征伐滅難陀而建國。第二層是孔雀帝國自身的地理需求：摩揭陀的財富在恆河與德干，而西北邊疆的商路、馬群與通往中亞的通道掌握在別人手上；犍陀羅與帕羅帕米薩德一帶是象、馬與象牙貿易的關鍵地帶，孔雀必須把它握在手裡，帝國的物資才能西流。第三層是塞琉古的處境：他的東方帝國靠總督制拼湊而成，核心在美索不達米亞與波斯，距印度河數千里，實際控制力到河東岸便已稀薄；他需要一次遠征來證明邊界，同時取得印度產的戰象——那是希臘世界唯一無處可買的軍力。最後一層是雙方都需要盟友：塞琉古西線要面對安提柯，孔雀則需要一位能擋住西來的馬其頓式軍團的君主。於是這場邊界衝突的結局不是消滅對方，而是把兩個人綁在同一張條約上，兩套帝國制度也由此第一次在同一條河流邊互相承認。
causeEn: There are four layers to the cause. The deepest is the vacuum Alexander left behind. When he died in 323 BC the empire was split among the successors, and the satrapies of the upper Indus, governed by Macedonians and Greeks, became for a while ownerless; the Greek sources say that the Indians shook off the burden of servitude by murdering their own governors, and order broke down with them, and Chandragupta rose in northwestern India in the middle of that disorder, spending eleven years of campaigning to end the Nanda line and found his state. The second layer is the geographical need of the Mauryan empire itself. The wealth of Magadha lay along the Ganges and the Deccan, while the trade routes, the horse herds and the corridors to Central Asia were in other hands; the region of Gandhara and the Paropamisadae was the key belt for elephants, horses and ivory, and the Mauryan state had to hold it for the wealth of the empire to flow westward. The third layer is the position of Seleucus. His eastern empire had been pieced together by satrapies, with its core in Mesopotamia and Persis thousands of kilometres from the Indus, and his real authority grew thin by the eastern bank; he needed a campaign to assert the frontier and to obtain the Indian war elephants, the one military asset the Greek world could buy nowhere else. The last layer is that both sides needed a partner. Seleucus had Antigonus in the west to face, and the Mauryan state needed a king who could hold off a Macedonian-style army coming from the west. The result of the border clash was therefore not the destruction of either side, but the binding of the two men into one treaty, and the first mutual recognition of two imperial systems on the banks of the same river.
impact: 這場戰爭的長期影響，遠大於它本身的軍事規模。第一，它把世界分成東西兩半：此後希臘式的王國在愛琴海與西亞，孔雀式的王國在次大陸，兩者之間是印度河這條界線；所謂印度河條約成為古代最著名的跨文化外交範本，割地、聯姻、贈象三件事同時辦成，後來希臘化諸王與東方王國的每一次結盟都照這個樣板辦。第二，戰象的轉移改變了地中海的戰局：塞琉古帶著五百頭象回西亞，公元前301年的伊普索斯之戰裡，這批象在方陣對撞中撞散安提柯的正面，塞琉古因此重奪亞洲；沒有這批象，繼承者戰爭的走向很可能不同。第三，孔雀帝國由此確立在南亞的絕對優勢，直到前185年巽伽王朝弒君篡位之前，北方邊界始終維持在印度河一線，孔雀的實際控制沒有越過喜馬拉雅與興都庫什。第四，這個結局的反面在整整一百年後顯現：前205年左右，塞琉古王安條克三世率軍東征，想收回這片失地，結果在印度河上游再遭挫敗，被迫退回；同一批被割掉的土地，最終落入中亞的安息與巴克特里亞之手。孔雀在這場戰爭裡替自己定下了邊界，卻沒有為塞琉古保住任何東西。第五，犍陀羅在割讓之後進入孔雀的保護網，後來成為希臘化藝術與佛教融合的中心，希臘式的寫作與造像技藝在那一帶落地生根，這是這條邊界線在文化上留下的長尾。
impactEn: The long consequences of this war were far greater than its military scale. The first is that it divided the world in two: from then on there were Greek-style kingdoms in the Aegean and the West, and a Mauryan-style kingdom on the subcontinent, with the Indus between them as the line. What came to be called the treaty of the Indus became the most famous model of diplomatic practice across cultures in the ancient world, accomplishing three things at once, a cession of land, a marriage and a gift of elephants, and every later alliance between the Hellenistic kings and the courts of the East was modelled on it. The second is that the transfer of the elephants changed the balance in the Mediterranean. Seleucus took five hundred of them back west, and at the battle of Ipsus in 301 BC they broke the front of Antigonus in the collision of the phalanges, and by that victory Seleucus recovered Asia; without those elephants the course of the Wars of the Diadochi would probably have run differently. The third is that the Mauryan empire was thereby confirmed as the dominant power of South Asia. Until the Shunga dynasty seized the throne by killing the last Maurya king in about 185 BC, the northern frontier stood on the Indus, and Mauryan control did not push past the Himalaya or the Hindu Kush. The fourth is that the reverse of this outcome became visible exactly a century later: around 205 BC the Seleucid king Antiochus III marched east to recover the lost lands, was defeated once more on the upper Indus, and was forced back; the very territories given up here eventually fell to the Parthians and the Bactrians of Central Asia. The Mauryan state fixed its own frontier in this war and kept nothing for Seleucus. The fifth is cultural. Gandhara, once ceded, entered the protective network of the Mauryan empire and later became the great meeting place of Hellenistic art and Buddhist imagery, where Greek writing and the Greek techniques of image-making took root; that is the long tail this frontier line left behind.
result: 結果沒有明確的勝方，這一點必須先說清楚。現存四家記載都只寫渡河、交戰、然後議和，沒有任何一位古代作者把塞琉古或旃陀羅笈多寫成這場戰爭的明確勝者；學者 Jansari 因此警告，關於會戰或衝突的細節太少，無法重建，Wheatley 與 Heckel 則據此認為戰事既不長久也不慘烈。無論如何，結果落在三條可確定的條款上：第一，塞琉古把帝國最東端的總督區——犍陀羅、帕羅帕米薩德、伽得羅西亞東部，可能還有阿拉科西亞與阿里亞——讓給旃陀羅笈多，孔雀的疆界因此西推到達什卡河與興都庫什山麓；第二，旃陀羅笈多贈給塞琉古五百頭印度戰象，這批象成為塞琉古在伊普索斯取勝的關鍵；第三，兩國以聯姻結盟，最可能的形式是旃陀羅笈多迎娶塞琉古的女性親屬。從大歷史看，這是一場孔雀完勝的邊境談判：塞琉古放棄的是他守不住的遠方土地，換回的是西線的時間與五百頭象；旃陀羅笈多以一個總督區換來對印度河上游的主動權，使孔雀帝國成為次大陸唯一的主人。這場戰爭的實際終點不是某座城池被攻下，而是兩條界線被一紙條約畫定：北線在孔雀與巽伽兩朝維持在印度河與興都庫什，直到公元前後的貴霜帝國越過中亞才被突破；而西線的那一半，在塞琉古手裡只維持到百年之後，便被安條克三世的失敗連同整片河外之地一起丟掉。
resultEn: There was no clear victor, and that must be said first. All four surviving accounts speak only of a crossing, a war and a settlement, and not one of the ancient authors presents either Seleucus or Chandragupta as the unambiguous winner of this war; Jansari accordingly warns that there is very little detail about the fighting and that it cannot be reconstructed, while Wheatley and Heckel take the degree of friendship between the two states to mean that the hostilities were probably neither prolonged nor grievous. Be that as it may, the result is fixed by three terms that can be stated with confidence. First, Seleucus ceded the easternmost satrapies of his empire, Gandhara, the Paropamisadae, the eastern part of Gedrosia and possibly Arachosia and Aria as well, to Chandragupta, and the Mauryan frontier was thereby pushed west to the foothills of the Hindu Kush and the Jhelum. Second, Chandragupta gave Seleucus five hundred Indian war elephants, and those animals became the key to Seleucus's victory at Ipsus. Third, the two states were joined by a marriage alliance, most probably in the form of Chandragupta taking a female relative of Seleucus to wife. Seen in the large, this was a border negotiation won outright by the Mauryan state: Seleucus gave up distant territory he could not hold and bought back time in the west together with five hundred elephants, while Chandragupta gave one satrapy for the initiative on the upper Indus and made the Mauryan empire the single master of the subcontinent. The real end point of this war was not a captured city but two lines drawn on a treaty. The northern line stood on the Indus and the Hindu Kush through the Maurya and Shunga houses, and was not broken until the Kushan empire crossed Central Asia around the turn of the era; the other half of that line, the part Seleucus kept, lasted barely a century before it was lost together with the whole country beyond the river in the failure of Antiochus III.
